generic.note: the fallback for every port set with no row — today's Classic layout, unchanged

rows.note: one-player cabinet: wheel, two pedals, a four-position gearbox and VR1-4 in a row. Gears sit on the face diamond by position — GEAR 1 south (B), 2 west (Y), 3 north (X), 4 east (A). The d-pad carries VR1-4 clockwise from Up; the cabinet has them left-to-right and a d-pad is not a row.

buttons.label: GEAR N
buttons.why: GEAR N: the pad is out of buttons, and neutral is reachable by shifting down out of gear 1

rows.note: tank cabinet: wheel, one pedal, six buttons. The buttons keep the generic row's order, so nothing a player has learned moves and only the wording arrives. Two controls the generic row cannot describe: BRAKE is an IPT_AD_STICK_Y, i.e. the left stick's Y axis and not a trigger, and there is no IPT_PEDAL2 at all, so L2 does nothing and is left unlabelled.

buttons.label: Button 7
buttons.why: the machine declares no IPT_BUTTON7 — leaving it on the L2 threshold, as the generic row does, binds a button that does not exist

buttons.label: Button 8
buttons.why: no IPT_BUTTON8 either; the accelerator on R2 is IPT_PEDAL and is bound outside the layout

rows.note: three buttons: Hold / Punch / Kick

Winning Run — wheel, gas/brake pedals, up/down gearshift on the d-pad.
Star Blade — analog aim on the left stick, fire on B.
Cyber Sled — twin-stick tank; missile/gun/view on the face buttons, left stick aims.
Armadillo Racing — trackball cabinet; the two dev-service buttons are a CUSTOM port, not player controls.
Air Combat 22 — flight stick + throttle; the throttle (AD_STICK_Z) defaults onto the right stick's X axis, not a trigger.

Alpine Racer / Alpine Racer 2 — two independent leg-lean axes (Steps Swing / Steps Edge), tagged P1/P2 like Cyber Sled's treads; reuses the single-pad twin-stick binding so the second leg lands on the right stick's X axis. P1 Left/Right are unnamed digital fields on the same port.
Alpine Surfer — same leg-lean pair as Alpine Racer.
Aqua Jet — MAME gives no PORT_NAME for the paddle, pedal or AD_STICK_Y fields; labelled by best-guess function pending a hand-check.
Cyber Commando — twin-stick mech cabinet, same shape as Cyber Sled (System 21); trigger/missile/view are placed on both physical sticks so either hand fires.
Cyber Cycles — leaning-motorcycle cabinet; throttle grip and brake lever share the pedal axes.
Prop Cycle — flying-bicycle cabinet; the pedal axis (AD_STICK_Z) defaults onto the right stick's X axis.
as ridgerac, with an added View Change button
lightgun cabinet, same shape as vcop; Foot Pedal is Time Crisis's cover/reload pedal, put on A for a pad player
Tokyo Wars — tank sim: wheel + two pedals (forward/backward) + twin cannon triggers; not a lightgun cabinet despite the name.
Sky Target — flight shooter; machine gun and missile on the face buttons, view change on X, aim on the left stick.
Top Skater — skateboard cabinet; jumps on the face buttons, board slide on the left stick.
two-player simultaneous cabinet; aim on the left stick, fire on B, missile on A. MAME leaves button 1 unnamed. Player 2 uses its own pad.
Sega Water Ski — slide on the left stick; Pitch Left/Right on the shoulders (natural L/R), Set on B, Select Up/Down on Y/X. No single clear primary action — outlier.

Air Combat (System 21) — flight stick on the left stick, throttle (AD_STICK_Z) on the right stick X (as airco22). MAME names none of the six buttons; placed by number (btn1→B, btn2→A …). By airco22's shape btn1 is likely Gun and btn2 Missile — needs a hand-check.

Wave Runner — jet-ski racer; handlebar steering on the left stick, View on X. Throttle is an analog lever (AD_STICK_Y), not a pedal, so it routes to the left-stick Y and cannot honour accelerator-on-R2. Only one button on the cabinet.

Cyber Troopers Virtual-On — twin DIGITAL sticks (both analog sticks drive them). Left/Right Shot on the shoulders, Left/Right Dash on the triggers (no pedals on this set, so the trigger axes are free). Symmetric twin-stick, so the single action/secondary rule doesn't apply — outlier.
The House of the Dead — lightgun cabinet, same shape as vcop. On a pad the trigger is button 1 and aim is the left stick. Two players; player 2 uses its own gun/pad.

Dynamite Baseball — digital stick for movement, two buttons on B/A, and the analog Bat Swing pedal (IPT_PEDAL), which lands on R2 as every pedal does. Two-player; player 2 uses its own pad. MAME leaves the two buttons unnamed.

Power Sled — networked sled racer (two-player master/slave cabinet; the network is not emulated). Gas/brake pedals land on R2/L2 as every driving game's do. The four buttons are the cabinet's network/entry controls, not gameplay actions: Entry on B, Call on A, the two Cancel buttons on Y/X. No steering axis is declared.
